blinding_guess.why: The code's use of the statistics types matches the humble statistics_msgs definitions (MetricsMessage fields metrics_source, measurement_source_name, unit, window_start, window_stop, statistics all exist; StatisticDataPoint.data is float64 and is formatted with std::to_string; data_type is uint8 and indexes a 6-entry label table); the /statistics topic is configured consistently for publisher and listener. The only irregularity seen (std_msgs used without a package.xml/CMake dependency) is outside the listed elements.

notes: topic_statistics_demo defines no interfaces; statistics_msgs/MetricsMessage and statistics_msgs/StatisticDataPoint (and the StatisticDataPoint.data field) are defined by the dependency statistics_msgs, so the three msg/field elements are in not_declared and also in references (the listener reads them). Their ports carry the dependency definition hash fetched from ros2/rcl_interfaces at tag 1.2.0 (byte-identical at 1.2.1 and at the humble branch); sha256_normalised is a proxy for the ROS 2 type hash and covers only each file's own text. The package provides /statistics indirectly: display_topic_statistics enables rclcpp topic statistics on the chatter subscription (SubscriptionOptions.topic_stats_options: state Enable, publish_topic default "/statistics", publish_period default 5000 ms, i.e. rate_hz 0.2), so rclcpp creates the MetricsMessage publisher inside this process; both topic name and period can be overridden at run time with --publish-topic / --publish-period (display_topic_statistics.cpp:82-88). The same process subscribes to publish_topic with TopicStatisticsListener (MetricsMessage, QoS history depth 10, topic_statistics_listener.cpp:36-38); that subscription is not recorded as a separate port. The header default topic_stats_demo::STATISTICS_TOPIC_NAME is the relative name "statistics" (topic_statistics_listener.hpp:25) but main always passes publish_topic explicitly. QoS of the /statistics publisher is null: the code sets no qos in topic_stats_options, the publisher is created inside rclcpp, and rclcpp source is not among the allowed sources, so the API default cannot be cited here; from recollection (unverified) the default is either the subscription's QoS or SystemDefaultsQoS, whose reliability/durability are chosen by the RMW configuration outside the snapshot. QoS and rate are not applicable to the msg/field elements and are null there. units: MetricsMessage carries its unit per message in the string field 'unit' (definition comment: 'e.g. percent, mb, seconds'), so no fixed unit is recorded. Outside the listed elements: std_msgs/String is used (string_talker_listener_nodes.hpp:23) but std_msgs is not declared in package.xml or found in CMakeLists.txt.
